chapter: Studio recordings of the late twenties and thirties
title: Backing singers: Johnny Marvin and the Boswell Sisters
summary: Kline lists the vocalists Morehouse accompanied; he worked for the Boswell Sisters six or seven years and for Johnny Marvin played whatever he played.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them

blocks.x: Uh huh. You did for a while in the thirties, you recorded behind a lot of vocalists, a lot of singers.
One after the other. Connie Boswell and the Boswell Sisters, Dick Robertson and Ed Henshaw, Johnny Morgan, Ethel Waters, Steve Washington, Chick Bullock. You did a lot of recordings - Chick Bullock.
Anyway these are a bunch of recordings that you made with vocalists. Johnny Marvin was a Texas ukulele player. Do you remember him?
You do remember Johnny Marvin. How do you play, how did a jazz band play behind a Texas singer. He was a Texas guitarist and ukulele player. Do you remember playing for him?
Well he would play what he would play.
And you would play what you were playing.
We would play what we were playing.
Let me ask you, some of these other people what you remember anything about them. For instance the Boswell Sisters, Connie Boswell.
The Boswell Sisters, I worked for them for six or seven years.
What kinds of music did they - that wasn't jazz so much was it?
Well it wasn't jazz so much but there was jazz in it.
